one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings fall inside the window. MarketBeat and Investing.com list Mon 2026-10-26, which matches past schedules but is not yet confirmed by the company. Guidance is $1.595-1.625B revenue and $2.01-2.07 non-GAAP EPS; Zacks consensus is $2.04 and $1.61B. Cadence has beaten in each of the last four quarters and the $8.1B backlog backs the quarter, so a miss is unlikely. The move will come from tone: early hints on 2027, China (15% of Q2 revenue), and AI monetisation. Management said on the Q2 call that it is 'very careful about projecting' next year and that H2 margins are modestly lower because of Intel and Hexagon investment. My new price data changes the picture of where the stock stands. It did not bounce from about $305, as my capped run assumed. It closed at $273.96 on 2026-09-15 and has rallied 28% in 12 sessions to $350.73, including a +6.2% day on 2026-10-01. That day followed Synopsys's investor day (FY27 revenue guide +15%, AWS $1B+ IP deal, OpenAI partnership; SNPS up about 13%) and the Micron beat. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: momentum and the Synopsys read-through support the stock, while reversal after a near-vertical 28% move and the earnings gap argue against it. Last quarter Synopsys beat and raised and still fell, and CDNS fell 3% in the two days after its own Q2 beat (Jul 28-29). With no informed directional edge, I keep the median at about $350.5, a hair below spot to allow some give-back of a low-volume one-day jump. I use sigma 0.125, above the usual 41%/3.5 = 11.7%, for the earnings gap and the recent realised swings, and the spread stays symmetric.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E (NTM EPS at the Oct-2027 horizon of about $10.6 x 34x) = $360, plus 40% FCF yield (2027E FCF of $7.45/share at a 2.2% yield) = $339. The blend is about $352, roughly spot. New evidence (consensus 2027 EPS $9.43-9.56, Synopsys's mid-teens industry outlook, a 30x-38x trading range within one month) supports keeping these inputs.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 (Q4'27-Q3'28) about $10.6 x 34x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of the two consensus prints, which agree within 1.5%.

$9.50 x (0.25 + 0.75 x 1.155) = $10.6. I take 2028 growth of 15.5%, slightly below the 16% consensus 2026-27 EPS growth (source 34) as a skeptic haircut. Synopsys's FY26-30 model of mid-teens revenue and mid-20s EPS CAGR (source 27) suggests the industry could beat this. Cadence management said margins improve into 2027 (source 26).

The five-year average is about 44x and spot is about 41x on TIKR's NTM (sources 4 and 39). In the last month the stock traded at about 30x NTM ($273.96 on Sep 15 vs about $9.2 NTM, source 20) and about 38x at today's close. That shows the multiple, not earnings, drives the price. Oppenheimer's Perform view calls the stock 'already full' on 2027 earnings and cites GAAP margin erosion (source 24). TIKR's own exit-multiple model uses 34x (source 39). I keep 34x as a lasting AI-disruption and decelerating-growth discount.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF of about $2.05B / 275M shares = $7.45/share at a 2.2% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Buybacks at about 50% of FCF (about $200M per quarter) roughly offset SBC dilution and the 3.2M shares issued for Hexagon (source 35).
2026 FCF of about $1.76B (OCF $2.0B less $240M capex) grown about 16%. That is consensus 2027 revenue growth of 12.9% (source 34) plus margin recovery after the H2-2026 investment period (source 26).

Today's yield on 2026 FCF is about 1.8% ($1.76B / ~$97B). I widen it to 2.2% because SBC is about 9-10% of revenue (GAAP operating margin 28% vs non-GAAP 45%; GAAP EPS guide $4.81 vs $8.10), so FCF overstates owner earnings (sources 1, 7, 8).

bear.story: AI-agent seat compression or open-source and startup flows (Kimi K3 follow-ups now close timing at 900 MHz post-route on 45nm; ChipAgents and Cognichip are funded) start to show in 2027 renewals. Alternatively, China tightens further: 15% of revenue, cloud-EDA licensing reportedly expanded in mid-2026, and Synopsys taking the marquee AI deals (OpenAI, AWS) signals share loss in IP and agents. 2027 EPS lands near $8.8, and the multiple compresses to about 26-27x NTM. September showed that sentiment alone can take the stock to $274 (30x), so fundamental damage puts it below the 52-week low, around $245.

base.story: Cadence delivers roughly consensus: 2027 EPS about $9.5, NTM about $10.6, revenue +13%. The backlog, hardware supply-constrained demand, and IP growth of 40% (largely organic) carry it. Synopsys's +15% FY27 guide confirms healthy industry demand. The disruption debate persists, so the multiple settles near 34x, below the 44x five-year average.

bull.story: Agentic tools are monetised through consumption and token pricing (SemiAnalysis cites about 20% renewal uplift; Synopsys now formally pitches subscription plus consumption), 2027 EPS beats to about $10.0-10.3, and NTM reaches about $11.2. The multiple re-rates to about 42x as the 'AI loser' narrative fades, as it partly did after Synopsys's investor day.

thesis_break_reason: I lowered this from $255. In September the stock closed at $273.96 (2026-09-15) on sector selling and rising yields, with no company-specific news, then recovered 28% in 12 sessions. A level only 7% below that low is too close to proven noise. $245 is about 7% below the $262.75 52-week low and about 25x my horizon NTM EPS ($9.8 NTM at the time), a multiple Cadence has not sustained in a decade. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break: a 2027 framework well below the $9.4-9.6 consensus, visible renewal or seat compression from AI agents, a broad loss of China licenses, or a backlog decline.

reasoning: With the search budget restored, I verified the capped-run inputs and closed its gaps. (1) Price path: Twelve Data closes show CDNS fell to $273.96 on 2026-09-15, not about $305 as I had inferred from Trefis. It then rallied 28% in 12 sessions, including +6.2% on Oct 1 after Synopsys's investor day (FY27 revenue +15%, LT mid-teens growth, EPS CAGR in the mid-20s, AWS $1B+ IP deal, OpenAI partnership). The selloff was macro and sector-driven (yields, a 6% software rout on Sep 1), with no company news. (2) Consensus: 2027 EPS $9.43-9.56, revenue +12.9%; analyst PT $404-405, range $300 (Oppenheimer, Perform) to $470. Piper is Neutral at $349; the FBN initiation is Outperform $375. Weiss downgraded to Hold on Sep 25. (3) Skeptic search: no short-seller report and no new securities litigation (only the legacy Bell Semi patent suits). Credit is clean: Fitch A- stable, S&P BBB+, about $2.5B debt. The bear case is narrative and multiple, not solvency. New bear evidence: the Kimi K3 open-source flow was extended in August to 900 MHz post-route (still 45nm); ChipAgents ($134M raised, 120+ customers) and Cognichip ($93M) are funded; Synopsys, not Cadence, won the marquee OpenAI and AWS AI deals; a reported BIS cloud-EDA licensing rule is unverified, and China rose to 15% of revenue in Q2, so there is no visible damage yet. Insiders sold about $134M over 12 months, led by the CEO, with no buying at the lows. Mitigating evidence: SemiAnalysis and Diligence Stack argue that agents raise engine consumption, and Synopsys's guide shows industry demand intact. Net, the new evidence leaves fair value at about $352 (unchanged). I trim bear probability slightly (0.25 to 0.23) and move the bear price and thesis break lower ($250 to $245, $255 to $245), because September proved that sentiment alone reaches the $270s. I widen the 12-month sigma from 0.36 to 0.38 given the month's realised 30x-38x multiple swing. Scenario mean is about $362. The ladder is a lognormal with median about $357 and sigma 0.38, with a modestly fattened left tail (P >= 246 = 0.82 vs 0.836 lognormal) and a slightly thinned far right tail (multiple ceiling).
